title: Mecca, a valley of trade and idols
hookLine: the old House of Ibrahim stands in a dry valley ringed with idols, and the tribe of Quraysh keeps it

cards: A dry valley between bare hills. Ibrahim and his son Isma'il lifting stones, building a simple house for the worship of one God, praying: our Lord, accept it from us. That was day forty-two.
Now jump forward, many centuries. Same valley. Same house, the Ka'ba.
But look around it now. Idols, standing around the house built for One. Caravans rolling in loaded with goods.
Poets, traders, pilgrims, deals being struck. This is Mecca, just before the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is born. For the next few weeks, this path follows his life, starting here.

teach.b: Mecca, or Makkah, sits in a valley where almost nothing grows. The Qur'an remembers Ibrahim praying for it as a valley without crops, next to Allah's sacred House. So why live there?

Two reasons: water, from the well of Zamzam you met with Hajar on day forty, and the House itself. Pilgrims came to the Ka'ba, and where pilgrims come, trade comes. The tribe that kept the House was Quraysh.
They ran the pilgrim trade, fed and watered visitors, and sent caravans out; commentators say south toward Yemen in winter and north toward Syria in summer.

A short surah, the hundred and sixth, names Quraysh and their winter and summer journeys, then tells them, in Pickthall's words: “So let them worship the Lord of this House.” The Lord of this House, not the idols.
By now the house of Ibrahim was crowded with them: a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari says that years later there were three hundred and sixty idols around the Ka'ba.
The Qur'an names three goddesses worshiped there: al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat. Muslims call this age the jahiliyyah, the time of not knowing. But not everyone had forgotten.
A few people in Mecca, called hanifs, turned away from the idols and tried to follow the religion of Ibrahim, as best they knew it.
That's the valley: a trading town, rich and proud, clever with poetry and deals, with an old house at its center, still standing, still visited, still waiting to be what it was built for.

how: Muslims face the Ka'ba in Mecca in every prayer, and travel there for hajj and 'umrah, walking around the House that Muslims believe Ibrahim and Isma'il built.

games.q: you're a Meccan trader before the Prophet's time. pilgrims come for the House, and you profit from every one. Surah Quraysh will later tell your tribe what to do. what is it?
o: worship the Lord of this House.
leave the valley for better land.
games.why: so let them worship the Lord of this House, who hath fed them against hunger and hath made them safe from fear (106:3–4).

practice: Walk slowly, in your mind, through a place you knew before it changed: a grandparent's house before it was sold, your street before the new buildings, a church, mosque or temple before it was renovated, a room before someone moved out.

What did it smell like, what was it for, and what is it for now? Some things change on the outside and keep their purpose; some lose it and wait. If you pray, you can remember that place with gratitude.

wordCard.voice: Mecca. Makkah: the dry valley of Ibrahim's House, a trading town kept by Quraysh, crowded with idols, where the Prophet ﷺ would be born.
